transcript_tail.text:
Recap:
- **#29** — already `Done` on board #2; PR #30 merged. No nudge needed (worker's heads-up was a false alarm — `gh` token actually has `project` scope here).
- **#31** filed: [[AH][supervisor] dispatch fresh sessions seeded with prior context (handoff, not resume)](https://github.com/jdtogni78/ai-harness/issues/31) — composes `new-session` + `sessions submit` (the same dispatch pattern I used on #29), gated by `RESUME_ON_RESTART=handoff|off`, with TTL + archived markers from #30 already filtering noise. On board, `Todo`.
- Saved the "handoff > resume for broken sessions" preference as a feedback memory so future recovery designs default the right way.

Want me to dispatch a worker on #31 the same way (oneoff in `~/dev/ai-harness` + manager-pattern kickoff), or hold off?
I want you to act as a manager, and dispotch work to sessions, and comm with them as they go

Manager mode on. Plan:
1. Dispatch #31 right now (extends the rehydrate.py from PR #30, owns its area cleanly)
2. Surface what else on board #2 is dispatch-ready in parallel, you pick the next ones to fan out
3. Coordinate replies via send-to-session as workers ping back (auto-invokes this session)

Let me verify the new combined `--wait --prompt` dispatch (it's faster than my old spawn-then-submit dance), then launch.
No `--wait --prompt` yet (skill description was ahead of the CLI). Going with the two-step pattern. Launching #31's worker.

Two things in flight. Quick answers, then I'll finish dispatching #31 and address your perm question fully.

**Short answer on perms across reboot**: No, I didn't change any permission configuration this turn. Workers run with `--permission-mode acceptEdits` (the supervisor's default), and the global `perm_gate` PreToolUse hook is in `ENFORCE=1 static-only` mode (per [[project_perm_gate]] — denies rm-rf/, asks on push/merge/deploy, auto-allows safe). That posture persists across reboot because it's file-based config, not session state. Nothing I did weakened or tightened it.

Now finishing the dispatch.

#31 worker is now in flight — `oneoff-mini-a591a365` / `cse_01Utk4EmrPekhoV2NaQtHEQT`, kickoff delivered (2160 chars). It'll claim, build, PR, and ping back via send-to-session.

**Fuller answer on the perm question.** Two layers to think about:

1. **Per-worker spawn flag.** Workers (both supervisor-managed `mm-*` and one-offs like the one I just spawned) are launched with `--permission-mode acceptEdits` — auto-allows safe edits, still prompts for Bash/destructive ops. This is set in code (`supervisor.py` / `new_session.py`) and persists across reboot. I didn't change it.

2. **Global `perm_gate` PreToolUse hook.** `ENFORCE=1` static-only — denies `rm -rf /`, asks on push/merge/deploy, auto-allows safe ([[project_perm_gate]]). File-based config; survives reboot. I didn't touch it.

So nothing got weaker or stronger this turn. But there's a real friction problem in manager-pattern dispatch you may be hinting at: **unattended workers can't answer "ask" prompts** (the picker UI is the answer channel, but nobody's looking). #31's worker is likely to hit at least the `git push` / `gh pr create` / merge prompts mid-flight, same as #29's did. Two non-mutually-exclusive levers:

- **Run `/fewer-permission-prompts`** to scan recent transcripts and add the manager-pattern primitives (`python3 -m remote_control *`, common git/gh subcommands) to project `.claude/settings.json`. Locked in across reboot. Conservative — only adds to the allowlist, doesn't touch the perm_gate hook.
- **Tune `perm_gate`'s static allow/deny lists** (the follow-up tracked in #25). Bigger surgery; out of scope unless you want it.
